title: Case: International parcel has produced four out-for-delivery notices and no delivery
context: A recipient is waiting for an international parcel, DL-4039, that arrived in the country at the end of June. He has stayed home on each day the carrier notified him it was out for delivery.
initial_request: Notice number four has landed. 'Out for delivery today.' I have now spent four days of annual leave watching a van not arrive, which is not how I pictured my summer. Before I ring work and burn a fifth: is it on a van today or isn't it? A yes or a no will do.

Urgent, DL-4039. Yesterday at 11:45 you told me this parcel has been in the import hold cage, bay C, since 06-29 with an import hold flag, and has never been loaded. At 16:15 Import billing told me the charges were paid in full on 06-30, there is no hold from their side and the parcel is released. This morning at 06:58 the recipient received a fourth out-for-delivery notice. Those three things cannot all be right. Could you check now whether the hold flag is still showing against DL-4039 on your system, and whether the parcel is physically on a van today or still in the cage? If the flag is still there, please say so plainly so I can take it back to Import billing. The recipient has taken four days off work for four notices and is deciding this morning whether to take a fifth.

must_not: Sends another message to Destination depot, Sedgemoor Arc Logistics restating the request already sent
Sends the customer a new promise, date or outcome that nobody has confirmed
Tells Xanthe the parcel is out for delivery today or that he should stay in, on the strength of the notification.
Tells Xanthe the parcel has been released or will definitely be delivered on a given day, on the strength of Import billing's reply alone.
Tells Xanthe charges are still owed or asks him to pay or prove payment again.
Sends Xanthe a stock reply that tracking shows out for delivery and to allow until 18:00.
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2404: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 728 days. The desk's correct action was already sent (event 10) and the last message is an acknowledgement or FYI with no request, so nothing is owed. 49 irrelevant events turn this into a long thread; the decisive events are the seed's.
